style: Refine every catalog object toward warm, softly lit cartoon art, consistent with the selected plant reference. Preserve identity, function and original palette family. Keep registered camera, dimensions, roots, sockets, ports, footprints and animation timing. No preferred horizontal light direction for rotatable world sprites; no directional ground shadows. Real 3D render output, editable Blender sources. The source 2D effects remain explicitly identified as 2D. Each object receives fresh independent editor/judge agents. Publish object-by-object to the same PR preview; integrate approved sprites into Godot after catalog review checks. Follow-on design exploration: improve the modeling itself, including forms, proportions, structure, crafted details and decorations. Original part counts and awkward geometry are not constraints. The editor may rebuild native geometry to achieve the better design; the judge should reward useful improvements. Preserve the locked registration, gameplay contact/clearance, animation and modular continuity contract. See modeling-policy.json version2.

outcomes.outcome: Ellis reads as a softly rounded, crafted cartoon chef in all four facings: the cap has a coherent crown/fold/brim relationship, head and ears have gentle volume, sleeves and palms feel soft, and the apron follows the torso as clothing. The broad cap and torso planes show curvature and thickness rather than looking like stacked rectangular blocks.
visibleChecks: At logical192x320, cap, ginger curls, face, ivory coat, orange apron and dark shoes remain distinct.
E/W profiles and N back view have intentional forms; improved curls may vary in size and arrangement instead of retaining the source pellet grid.
Construction and proportion improvements remain inside the locked scale/contact/animation contract; neither original part count nor original silhouette is an aesthetic pass condition.

outcomes.outcome: Keep recognizable Ellis identity: light golden skin, ginger curls, round black glasses, navy cap, ivory coat, orange/amber apron and necktie, and dark shoes. Skin appears warm and light; the navy cap remains navy with readable lit volume.
visibleChecks: Glasses stay visibly round and black while eyes, brows and friendly smile remain legible through/around them in the front view.
Orange clothing, ginger hair and warm skin remain distinguishable through value/material/shape; the coat retains an ivory body rather than becoming clipped white or gray.
The separate family concept is a style reference, not authority to replace Ellis with another chef identity.

outcomes.outcome: Broad soft highlights and gentle occlusion describe the cap, face, curls and garments with warmth and depth. Dark glasses and shoes retain clean shape, and cap/hair recesses do not become black dead areas.
visibleChecks: One shared native light/material setup works for S/E/N/W without per-facing color correction.
Rotated views have comparable warmth and readable values, with no preferred horizontal illumination direction.
Avoid hard directional ground shadows, blown coat/skin patches, tiny distracting specular flecks, crushed undersides, and bright rim halos.

outcomes.outcome: Use restrained material and structural detail to make Ellis feel finished: readable garment layering, collar/cuffs, apron straps/waist/pocket or fastening, and cap edge/fold detail. Rounded curls read as hair masses and glasses read as a deliberate frame rather than faceted dark polygons.
visibleChecks: Details support silhouette and garment construction at logical use size; stitches or fabric texture may be subtle or omitted if they turn into noise.
Skin, hair, cloth, glasses and metal knife have coherent distinguishable responses; finish need not be glossy.
Purposeful additions are welcome; reproducing every target seam, rivet, stitch, or microtexture is not required.

outcomes.outcome: Every exported frame remains clean and readable at logical size and enlarged on light, neutral gray and dark backgrounds. No required facing or action frame has a material defect or dead spot.
visibleChecks: No popping/tearing at elbows, wrists, headwear, glasses, hair or apron; no detached decorations, coplanar flicker, abrupt shading seams, or changing topology.
No unintended clipping between cap and hair, frames and face, hands and coat/apron, or held props and native geometry.
Transparent edges have no white/colored matte fringe, detached alpha specks, or unwanted shadow.
Intentional source occlusion is allowed: the salmon is hidden behind the body in N; unseen views need coherent native design, not invented target evidence.

outcomes.outcome: Preserve the authored motion and functional registration while giving the refined forms convincing continuity. Idle has its existing subtle bob/hand movement, work keeps the cooking/knife action, hold retains the separately composed dish, and load keeps the original out-and-back presentation gesture.
visibleChecks: Feet remain planted and body/root registration remains stable as in the source.
The 2D salmon stays attached to the source palm-midpoint path with its original visibility and yaw cancellation; the native3D knife follows the right palm during work.
Load remains non-looping metadata with twelve samples; dish remains visible through the ending frame. Do not introduce a release, belt transfer path, walking, or a new station animation.
Garment/cap/hair improvements follow the authored rig with no sliding or frame-specific fitting.
